structure.summary: The text covers India's economic growth to $4T GDP, driven by demographic dividend, urbanization, and digitalization. It details rising disposable incomes (up 50% in five years), demographic impact of Millennials and Gen Z, growing income disparity with top 10% earning 57% of national income, and changing customer preferences toward aspirational, convenient, personalized, and ethical products. structure.title: Strategic Overview
structure.summary: Trent's strategic overview outlines a business strategy centered on building consumer brands, leveraging its platform, and delivering resilient financial outcomes through own brands, quality, and nimble responsiveness. Key strategic priorities include reach, availability, look and feel, brand portfolio, and differentiation. The playbook emphasizes direct-to-consumer distribution, control of consumer touchpoints, avoiding discounting, and owning the consumer image. It highlights strong product disciplines, speed to market, and an allocation/replenishment model. Expansion targets Tier 2/3 cities and metro areas, focusing on proximate market share and store portfolio quality. Trent is investing in technology, automation, and supply chains (e.g., RFID, AI/ML) to scale a portfolio of lifestyle brands, strengthen core efficiencies, and drive premiumisation. The Star food business model with tight footprint, sharp pricing, and fresh focus is also covered, including own-branded offerings and value differentiation.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies for Income, Taxes, and Fixed Assets
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for interest income (accrual using EIR), dividends (recognized when right to receive is established), and rental income (straight-line over lease term). It details income taxes: current tax based on estimated taxable income with periodic evaluation of tax positions; deferred tax on temporary differences, including recognition, measurement, review, and offsetting. Property, plant and equipment are initially at cost, with freehold land not depreciated; subsequent measurement, impairment review, capitalization criteria, depreciation methods (straight-line for retail, written-down value for others) and useful lives per Schedule II, de-recognition, residual value review, capital work-in-progress, and low-cost asset policy. Finally, intangible assets are initially at cost, with finite-life assets amortized (software over 5 years) and reviewed for impairment, while goodwill and distribution network are indefinite-life and not amortized but reviewed annually.

nodes.title: g) Investment Property
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for investment property, non-current assets held for sale, borrowing costs, and leases. It defines investment property, initial and subsequent measurement, depreciation under IND AS 40, de-recognition, and review of residual values. It outlines criteria for classifying non-current assets as held for sale under IND AS 105. Borrowing costs directly attributable to qualifying assets are capitalized, while others are expensed. For leases as lessee, it details recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities, initial and subsequent measurement, remeasurement triggers, depreciation, impairment, presentation, variable rents, and the practical expedient for combining lease and non-lease components.

nodes.title: Investment Property, Non-Current Assets Held for Sale, and Borrowing Costs
key_items: h) Non Current Assets Held For Sale
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for investment property, including subsequent expenditure capitalization, depreciation using the straight-line method per IND AS 40, useful lives of components (building 60 years, furniture 7/10 years, electrical installations 5 years, office equipment 5 years), de-recognition and gain/loss treatment, expensing of repair costs, and annual review of residual values, useful lives, and depreciation methods. It also details criteria for classifying non-current assets as held for sale under IND AS 105. Finally, it explains borrowing costs capitalization for qualifying assets, expensing of other borrowing costs, and inclusion of interest, other costs, and exchange differences.

nodes.title: Leases Company as lessee

Additionally, it summarizes policies on inventories (lower of cost or net realizable value), impairment of non-financial assets (recoverable amount, reversal), provisions (recognition, reimbursement), contingencies (disclosure thresholds), and employee benefits (defined contribution and defined benefit plans, gratuity, long-term incentive plan, other retirement benefits).

nodes.title: Accounting Policies: Leases, Sale-Leaseback, Inventories, Impairment, Provisions, Contingencies, Employee Benefits
nodes.summary: The page outlines key accounting policies: as lessor, leases are classified as finance or operating, with rental income recognized straight-line; sale and leaseback transactions follow Ind AS 116, recognizing right-of-use assets and liabilities; inventories are valued at lower of cost or net realizable value; non-financial assets are reviewed for impairment with reversals recognized; provisions are recognized for present obligations when outflow is probable; contingencies are disclosed unless remote; employee benefits include defined contribution and defined benefit plans, with gratuity and long-term incentive plans provided via actuarial valuation using the Projected Unit Credit Method, and actuarial gains/losses recognized in OCI or profit & loss as applicable.

nodes.title: Other Retirement Benefit

It details financial instruments: initial recognition/measurement of financial assets at fair value or amortized cost, subsequent measurement categories (debt at amortized cost, FVTOCI, FVTPL; equity at FVTOCI, FVTPL, or cost), derecognition, and impairment. It also covers non-derivative financial liabilities (FVTPL or other financial liabilities at amortized cost), derecognition of liabilities, offsetting of financial instruments, and significant accounting judgments, estimates, and assumptions.

nodes.title: Financial Instruments: Measurement, Derecognition and Impairment Policies
key_items: Equity Instruments measured at FVTOCI or FVTPL
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for financial assets and liabilities: initial recognition (trade date, transaction price for receivables without financing component); five subsequent measurement categories (debt at amortized cost, FVTOCI, FVTPL; equity at FVTOCI or FVTPL, and at cost per Ind AS 27); amortized cost using EIR; FVTPL residual category; irrevocable equity classification with OCI changes not recycled; derecognition of assets when rights expire or risks/rewards transfer, including continuing involvement guarantees; impairment assessment for objective evidence of loss events affecting future cash flows; non-derivative liabilities classified as FVTPL or other financial liabilities measured at amortized cost; and derecognition of liabilities on discharge, cancellation, expiry, or substantial modification with difference in P&L.

nodes.title: Offsetting of Financial Instruments
nodes.summary: The text covers offsetting of financial instruments, requiring net reporting when enforceable legal right and intention to settle net exist. Note 3.1 discusses significant accounting judgments, estimates, and assumptions, including their basis on historical experience, ongoing review, and recognition of revisions. Specific judgments include provision for doubtful advances and trade receivables (no credit loss calculation under Ind AS 109 due to materiality, but judgment-based provisioning), loyalty points (nil breakage for deferred revenue), and defined benefit plans (actuarial valuation for gratuity and compensated absences using discount rate, salary increase, and mortality assumptions, highly sensitive to changes).

nodes.title: Fair Value measurement of Financial Instruments:

nodes.title: b) Fair value measurement
nodes.summary: The text covers fair value measurement and revenue recognition policies. Fair value is defined as the price in an orderly transaction between market participants, determined in the principal or most advantageous market. It discusses valuation assumptions, highest and best use for non-financial assets, and valuation techniques maximizing observable inputs. A three-level fair value hierarchy (Level 1, 2, 3) is described. Governance includes Board approval of policies and involvement of external valuers. Revenue recognition covers sale of goods (net of discounts, taxes, loyalty points), services, interest (EIR method), dividends, and rental income (straight-line basis).

nodes.title: d) Taxes on Income
nodes.summary: This text covers accounting for income taxes, detailing both current and deferred tax. Current tax is based on estimated taxable income and credits, includes tax on items recognized outside profit or loss, and involves periodic evaluation of tax return positions and offsetting of assets and liabilities when legally enforceable. Deferred tax is provided on temporary differences between tax bases and carrying amounts, with deferred tax assets reviewed and reduced if recovery is not probable, and liabilities recognized except for certain initial recognition exceptions. Unrecognized deferred tax assets are reassessed, and measurement uses expected tax rates. Deferred tax items are recognized in profit or loss, other comprehensive income, or equity, and offsetting is allowed under legal right.

nodes.title: e) Property, Plant and Equipment
nodes.summary: The text details accounting policies for Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE), Intangible Assets, Investment Property, Non-Current Assets Held for Sale, Borrowing Costs, and Leases. PPE is initially at cost, with freehold land not depreciated; depreciation methods (Straight Line or Written Down Value) and useful lives are specified, along with impairment review and de-recognition. Intangible assets are amortized over finite lives, while goodwill and distribution network are not amortized but tested for impairment. Investment Property is measured at cost, depreciated on Straight Line basis, and de-recognized similarly. Non-current assets held for sale are classified under IND AS 105. Borrowing costs directly attributable to qualifying assets are capitalized. Lease accounting covers recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities, initial and subsequent measurement, and remeasurement triggers.

nodes.title: Trent Limited Notes: Intangible Assets and Investment Property Accounting Policies
nodes.summary: The page presents accounting policies for capital work-in-progress, low-cost assets, and Nahar Retail's depreciation, followed by sections on intangible assets and investment property. Intangible assets are initially at cost; finite-life assets are amortized (e.g., software over 5 years) with impairment reviews, while goodwill and distribution network are indefinite and not amortized but reviewed annually. Gains/losses on derecognition go to profit or loss. Investment property, held for rentals or appreciation, is initially at cost with capitalized subsequent expenditure under conditions; depreciation is straight-line per Ind AS 40 (building 60 years; furniture/electrical 7/10 years; office equipment 5 years). Derecognition gains/losses are recognized in profit or loss, other costs expensed, and residual values, useful lives, and methods reviewed annually.

nodes.title: h) Non Current Assets Held For Sale
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for non-current assets held for sale under Ind AS 105, borrowing costs capitalization, and lease accounting for both lessee and lessor including right-of-use assets, lease liabilities, sale and leaseback transactions, and practical expedients. Significant accounting judgements, estimates, and assumptions are listed including doubtful advances, loyalty points, taxes, lease discounting, defined benefit plans, fair value measurement, impairment of financial assets, and control assessment.
